subject: FinLytics SLO qualification: token caps, streaming behavior, and PoC next steps
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Anna Gomez <anna@finlytics.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + performance SLOs discussed on call

Anna / Tom — thanks again for the deep dive today. Quick recap so we have a shared reference and clear next steps.

Key points from discovery:
- Primary user flow: real-time analyst assistant that ingests multi-document batches (avg 3–5 docs) and returns structured summaries + follow-ups.
- Typical prompt size: ~3.5–6k input tokens (plain text after extraction). Peak cases: up to ~45k tokens when including full report archives.
- Desired output: streamed partial summaries (first token out quickly), final output up to 2k tokens.
- Performance targets you called out: p95 end-to-end latency <= 500ms for short prompts (<512 tokens); streaming first-byte under 250ms; graceful degradation allowed for huge contexts but with clear user messaging.
- Concurrency: expected burst to 80 concurrent sessions during market open; steady-state 20–30 concurrent.
- Regional preference: primary in us-west, potential eu for EU customers.

Open questions we promised to validate on our side (see below for internal owners):
1) Impact of 32k vs 65k context windows on first-byte time and per-token CPU/GPU cost.
2) Whether incremental KV/prefix caching for repeated document contexts will keep steady-state latency within your target.
3) Suggested configuration (model variant, quantization, batching, cache TTL) to meet SLOs and cost envelope.

Attachments: FinLytics-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), SLO-draft.xlsx (rough SLO table).

Next steps / proposed PoC plan:
- Redwood to stand up a 2-week PoC on dedicated capacity using redwood-4x-32k-quant (approx config will be included in the PoC doc). PoC will include your sample prompts and the streaming endpoint so you can validate first-byte and end-to-end behavior.
- We'll instrument token-level latency and cost reporting and share dashboards.
- Goal: get a baseline for p50/p95/p99 latency across your short, median, and long prompt buckets.

I'll loop in engineering for the technical clarifications and aim to deliver estimated latency impact numbers for the 32k/65k scenarios by Tue.

Thanks —
Nikhil Sharma
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Anna Gomez <anna@finlytics.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@finlytics.com>, FinLytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + performance SLOs discussed on call

Thanks, Nikhil — very helpful recap. A few clarifications before we lock the PoC: 

1) For the "peak" 45k token cases: do you expect a hard cap or streaming fallback? Our UX needs to indicate progress and allow partial outputs if final generation exceeds a timeout.
2) Can you confirm whether your hosted offering supports prefix/KV caching across sessions for repeated contexts (we often run the same baseline report across many analyst queries)? If not, what are the estimated latency improvements with Dedicated + caching enabled?
3) Cost band: can you give a rough delta between hosted per-token pricing vs a dedicated reserved pool for our projected monthly token volume (~1.5B tokens)?

Procurement is cc'd — they want to understand timelines for an MSA and whether we should prepare a shorter pilot contract or a reserved monthly commitment.

Also: do you have any empirical numbers for first-byte time on 32k contexts when streaming is enabled? Even ballpark figures are fine for now.

Best,
Anna Gomez
Head of Product, FinLytics
anna@finlytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Quick recap + performance SLOs discussed on call — engineering ask

Dev / Jonas — forwarding FinLytics follow-ups. High level asks we need numbers for: 

- First-byte latency (stream start) estimates for model variants at these context sizes: 32k and 65k. Please provide p50/p95 for single-turn scenarios and for streaming (time-to-first-chunk). If you have microbenchmarks broken down by tokenizing/compaction, KV assembly, and initial kernel launch, include those numbers.
- Does our runtime support cross-request prefix/KV cache that can be shared across sessions for identical document contexts? If yes, what are the limitations (TTL, memory footprint per 10k tokens cached, eviction policy)?
- Expected throughput (tokens/s) and GPU memory pressure for the proposed redwood-4x-32k-quant and a redwood-4x-65k-quant variant.

We'd like a short, customer-friendly summary we can share with Anna that includes: recommended PoC config, likely latency envelopes for short/medium/long prompts, and an option A (hosted with dedicated pool) vs option B (private/VPC) tradeoffs.

Target: get a draft reply by EOD Wed so Nikhil can send to FinLytics on Thu.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Anna Gomez <anna@finlytics.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + performance SLOs discussed on call — PoC proposal & MAP

Anna / Tom — thanks for the quick reply and for looping procurement. Below is a concise PoC proposal and the mutual action plan (MAP). I've included the engineering notes from Jonas/Dev inline where relevant.

Executive PoC goal
- Validate streaming first-byte & end-to-end latency for your three prompt buckets (short <512, median ~4k, long >32k) and quantify cost/throughput tradeoffs so you can pick an operational model.

PoC scope (2 weeks) — config we propose
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) in us-west (option to add eu region later).
- Model: redwood-4x-32k-quant (we can test a 65k variant if you want, see tradeoffs below).
- Streaming: enabled with chunk size tuned to 128 tokens to minimize TTF while keeping overhead low.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching enabled for repeated contexts (Jonas notes: shared in-memory cache per GPU with TTL 30min, approx 1.2 GB per 10k tokens cached; eviction LRU-based).
- SLO instrumentation: token-level traces, per-request KV hit/miss, and p50/p95/p99 latency dashboards.

Engineering estimates (ballpark, from our internal microbenchmarks)
- 32k context (single-turn): first-byte (stream start) p50 ~120ms, p95 ~320ms; end-to-end for median 4k output payload p95 ~420ms when batching disabled and streaming chunk size 128.
- 65k context (single-turn): first-byte p50 ~220ms, p95 ~700ms; end-to-end p95 often exceeds 1s for large outputs unless prefix caching is effective.
- With prefix/KV cache hit (warm): we see first-byte improvements of ~35–60% depending on cache locality.

Cost/operational notes
- Dedicated pool: better predictability for bursts and cheaper per-token at scale (we'll provide committed pricing tiers in the next doc).
- Hosted (shared capacity) with burst: faster to stand up but price per token is higher and noisy neighbors can affect p95 tails.

Mutual action plan (MAP)
- This week: FinLytics to share 10 representative prompts (short/median/long), and mark the ones used for SLA validation — Anna to send by Fri 2/20.
- Redwood to provision PoC cluster (dedicated) and provide a test endpoint + dashboards by Mon 2/23.
- Week 1 of PoC: run baseline tests (no cache) and collect p50/p95/p99 for each bucket.
- Week 2 of PoC: enable caching and tuned chunking; compare delta and present final recommendations.
- Contracting: Procurement to indicate whether a 1–2 month pilot PO or a short-term reserved commitment is preferred; Redwood can draft a pilot addendum for MSA.

Attachments: technical-asks.md (engineering details and the two config options). Links: HubSpot record, shared Drive folder, NDA DocuSign above.

If this looks good I will send the official PoC quote and the project kickoff doc. Happy to jump on a 30m call tomorrow to go through priorities with procurement.

Talk soon —
Nikhil Sharma
